43 years after its last confirmed record, the similar firefly (Pyractomena similis) has been rediscovered in the United States.

This spring, it was documented in Virginia and Delaware. In Delaware, entomologist Christopher Heckscher spotted about eight to 12 fireflies at Brandywine Creek State Park. Their amber flashes and microscopic examination confirmed the species. Researcher Aljoscha Nern also documented a sighting in Ashburn, Virginia, on iNaturalist.

“Lost to science” means a species has gone undocumented, not that it is extinct. A recent review listed 28 firefly species in the United States and Canada as lost to science. Further surveys are needed to establish the range and population of P. similis.

🪙 THE YEAR SILVER LEFT AMERICA’S POCKET CHANGE

On July 23, 1965, President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Coinage Act of 1965. Until then, U.S. dimes, quarters and half dollars were 90 percent silver.

“When I have signed this bill before me, we will have made the first fundamental change in our coinage in 173 years,” Johnson said at the signing. The new dimes and quarters had no silver at all, just copper-nickel faces bonded to a copper core.

That is why collectors still check dates. A 90 percent silver dime holds about 0.072 troy ounce of pure silver, so $1 in face value of pre-1965 dimes or quarters holds about 0.72 ounce of silver.

💬 China supports diplomacy on Iran nuclear issue, urges return to talks: Envoy

📌 Tehran, IRNA – China’s ambassador to Tehran has reaffirmed Beijing’s support for a diplomatic solution to Iran’s nuclear issue, urging all sides to keep the door to negotiations open, de-escalate tensions, and return to dialogue.

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Cong Peiwu referred to rising regional tensions since the beginning of the year and stressed that Beijing would continue its efforts to support regional peace and stability in line with President Xi Jinping’s initiatives.
​
Highlighting the two countries’ deep-rooted friendly ties, he said Tehran-Beijing relations had developed in a sound and stable manner over the past 55 years despite regional and international changes, with considerable potential for further expansion.
​
Regarding Iranian nuclear issues, the ambassador said the history of the Iranian nuclear issue shows it could only be resolved through diplomacy. He described the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Iran and the US as a valuable outcome of mediation efforts.
​
Cong Peiwu stressed the need to keep the dialogue process on track, saying that now that the door to negotiations has been opened, it should not be closed, and that efforts to pursue peace should continue as long as there is hope. He added that the immediate priority is to de-escalate tensions and return to dialogue and negotiations.
​
He emphasized that China would continue its efforts to promote a political settlement of the Iranian nuclear issue and contribute to regional peace and stability, reaffirming Beijing’s commitment to its principled positions and support for Iran’s legitimate and reasonable rights.
​
Elsewhere in his remarks, the ambassador reaffirmed Beijing’s support for a political settlement in Yemen and respect for the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, calling for the swift restoration of peace and stability.
​
He also stressed the need for dialogue, mutual respect, and regional cooperation to establish a comprehensive and sustainable regional security framework, saying China is ready to work with the international community toward this goal.
